title: Al-Maamun and the Pyramids of Egypt
logline: A caliph digs into a pyramid for treasure, spends a fortune on a tiny tunnel, and finds gold worth exactly what the digging cost.
moral: Greed for what others built can cost as much as it gains; great monuments outlast kings, and wisdom is knowing when to stop.
tone: Dry comedy of accounts (the level scale, PROFIT 0) inside a tall, awed frame; the last third turns calm and reflective. No villains, no violence.

beats.summary: The pyramids are revealed by a camera tilt; he is astonished at the stones and the height.
He hears people talk of treasure hidden inside and wants to know what they hide.
He decides to open one pyramid and even to remove a large part of it.
The huge stones resist the tools: picks bounce and bend.
Many days pass and the pay chest empties on men, tools and hauling.
All of it buys only a small tunnel, and nothing appears.
Then money and treasure are found in the passage.
Weighed against the cost, the value equals the expenses exactly: no more, no less.
He realises he has gained nothing from the costly attempt.
He takes the find, drops the idea of demolition and orders the work stopped.
The tale praises the pyramids as wonders built of great stones set exactly.
Old storytellers imagine jewels, weapons, books and unseen guardians inside.
These are legends of the story, not confirmed history.
Kings and builders are gone; the pyramids remain, and al-Maamun stops seeking profit under them.

sets.description: pyramidSite view 'far' (new shared set, world 1000 x 1230, ground y 900, strip option w 1600 with camX). Sky by skyCycle(u) with o.sky false on Library dunes: reuse the far and mid dune layers of desertRoad (road:false, no palms) for the land. Great pyramid: apex (560, 250), base x 160..960 on y 900 (800 wide, 650 high), 13 courses 50 high drawn as horizontal course lines with staggered vertical joints every 100; sunlit left face flat yellow with red Ben-Day dots, right face (apex to x 960, split line apex to (650, 900)) a darker ochre with black dots. Two far pyramids behind on the left: B apex (190, 520) base x 20..360 on y 885; C apex (70, 690) base x -50..190 on y 890, both flat with only 4 course lines, parallax 0.6. Two Library palmTree at x 60 (h 260) and x 930 (h 220) for scale. Option scar: a small dark arch 26 wide x 30 high at (300, 900) on the left face of the great pyramid (the tunnel mouth, shown from S11 on).

pyramidSite view 'face': the bottom courses of the great pyramid seen close as a stepped wall, world 1000 x 1230. Sand ground from y 900 to 1230 (Library ground tone for sand, as desertRoad). Courses 170 high: tops at y 730, 560, 390, 220, 50; course n begins at x 300 + 90 n and runs off the right edge (a staircase edge on the left with sky and far pyramid C behind it). Blocks 260 wide with joints staggered by 130 on alternate courses; each block has its own seeded dot shading and one chipped corner here and there. Course 0 blocks: x 300..560, 560..820, 820..1080. The dig block is x 560..820, y 730..900. Field dig 0..1 on that block: 0 clean, 0.15 three chip marks, 0.4 a dent 70 wide, 1 an arched black opening 120 wide x 140 high centred x 690 with its floor on y 900, rubble of 6 seeded stones at its foot. Field outline 0..1: a red dashed rectangle x 480..1000, y 220..900 (the 'large part' he wants removed). People stand on the sand in front of the wall (feet y 900 to 930). At s 0.8 a person is 192 high: just taller than one block, which is the scale joke.

pyramidSite view 'section': cutaway of the great pyramid, world 1000 x 1230. Outline apex (500, 180), base x 60..940 on y 900; inside filled with dark brown stone, course lines every 48, blue-black dot shading; sky by skyCycle(u) outside, sand below y 900. Tunnel: a 60 high passage with a rough roof that enters the left face at (109, 820) (floor y 850) and runs horizontally; field len 0..1 puts its end at x 109 + 260 len (x 369 at len 1). Hidden niche: x 372..470, y 770..850, closed by a wall 12 thick at x 369..381 until field breach 0..1 opens it; holds the hoard. Field legend 0..1: three dashed chambers A (500, 560) 130 x 84, B (420, 690) 110 x 70, C (610, 740) 124 x 80 joined by dashed passages 30 wide (A to B, A to C, C down to (700, 900)); each chamber takes a content callback. Field solid 0..1 fills everything back to plain stone (the inside is unknown). Person scale inside the tunnel: s 0.24 (58 high); use a camera of about zoom 2.4 centred (300, 800) so the figure is about 135 px on screen.

The planned desertCamp reduced to what this film needs: night sky (skyCycle u 0.72) over two dune lines, the great pyramid as a flat navy silhouette (apex (700, 330), base x 400..1000 on y 880) with a yellow rim on its left edge from the moon, one striped tent at the left edge (x 0..220, top y 560), a small fire at (500, 905) (three flame shapes, flicker from K.noise, warm halftone disc r 200) and a carpet mat x 250..760, y 900..930. Storyteller sits at x 330, children at x 600 and x 700.

props.description: Pickaxe: brown shaft 150 x 9, grey double-pointed head 96 wide and 16 thick with a slight curve, black brush outline. Drawn about the grip point with rot. Field bend 0..1 curls one point up by 40 degrees (the stone wins). Placed at the worker's hands (P.hands) with rot from the strike cycle.
The planned shovel (AN-114, AN-131): shaft 150 x 8, blade 40 x 52; worker 2 leans on it.

The planned torch (AN-114): stick 70 long with a three-tongue flame and a yellow halftone light disc r 90 that reveals the tunnel walls (draw the tunnel dark, then the disc with globalCompositeOperation lighter or a clipped lighter redraw).
The planned coin mound (fill 0..1, single coin option). Used on the pay table, as flying coins, and on the scale.
The planned treasureHoard chest: 150 x 100, lid open 0..1, fill 0..1 (coins visible above the rim). The caliph's pay chest starts full (fill 1) in S6 and empties to 0.05.

The found treasure: the planned treasureHoard chest (110 x 76, old, grey-green with a broken lock) plus a coinPile and four planned jewels spilling beside it; goldGlow behind. Drawn at 0.5 scale inside the niche and at full size on the sand and on the scale.

The planned flat balance scale, large: post 230 high on a 160 wide foot, beam 380 wide pivoting at the post top with field tilt (radians, positive = right pan down), two pans 130 wide hanging on three chains 110 long that stay vertical. Stands on a low table (carpet covered box 420 x 60) at x 500.
The planned ledger (AN-138): account book 90 x 70 in the vizier's hands, open state with tally strokes that grow with a fill field; a reed pen in his other hand.

The planned priceTags running-total counter used as two tags in panel space: SPENT (red tag) and FOUND (yellow tag), each a coin icon and a number drawn with the style counter primitive. They count in purses of gold, 0 to 100.

Macro insert of a stone joint: two block corners filling the frame with a hairline joint between them; a dovetail (bow-tie) slot 220 wide x 90 high cut across the joint; a dark blue-grey iron clamp of the same shape drops into it; then a ladle (bowl 80 wide on a 200 long handle) pours pale grey lead that fills the gap round the clamp (fill 0..1, a wavy top edge until it sets flat, white steam puffs).

Three chamber contents at icon size (about 90 x 60 each): the planned jewels (four cut gems), weapons (the planned sword as two crossed scimitars over a round shield) and books (a stack of three with one open, squiggle lines). Each has a dashed-outline ghost state for the disclaimer.

scenes.summary: Arrival. The caliph rides into Egypt with his vizier; the camera lifts from the riders to the three pyramids.

camera.notes: Start low and close on the dunes with the pyramids out of the top of frame: {x 300, y 860, zoom 1.7} held 0 to 5.2; ease to the full world {x 500, y 615, zoom 1.0} from 5.78 to 7.9 so the great pyramid rises into view on the word.

actions.action: Holds his turban on with one hand as he leans back to see the top

actions.acting: teeth grit, eyes shut on impact (lid 1 for 3 frames)

Strike 3: the tip of his pickaxe curls up like a hook; he holds it up and stares at it
actions.acting: slow blink, gaze tool then camera [0, 0.05]

actions.action: A progress gauge pops at the top of the panel: a bar that creeps to about 3 percent and stops
Swings again but slower: the cycle time doubles, the lift sags

actions.action: Wipes his brow with his forearm and leans on the pick
Sits down on the sand with his back to the block
Pulls out to the full world: the caliph is tapping his foot, arms folded

scenes.summary: Many days and huge sums. The sun wheels over a fixed shot while the pay chest empties into men, tools and hauling; the SPENT counter runs up.

camera.notes: Locked full world so that only the sky, the shadows and the chest change: a time-lapse.

actions.action: SPENT tag pops with a coin icon and starts to count

actions.acting: gaze flicks chest, ledger, chest; brow -0.6

scenes.summary: After all that: only a small tunnel in the body of the pyramid, and nothing in it. Cutaway view.

camera.notes: Whole cutaway {x 500, y 615, zoom 1.0} from 53.68 so the tunnel looks tiny in the mass; push in to the tunnel {x 300, y 800, zoom 2.4} from 59.9 to 61.2 for the empty end.

The tunnel draws itself in from the face, slowing as it goes, and stops

actions.acting: torch disc flickers; w1 strike loop at small scale

Label TINY! pops beside the tunnel with a pointer
Pushes in to the tunnel end
actions.acting: the stone mass closes round the little passage

actions.action: Sweeps the torch left, right, up: bare stone everywhere
actions.acting: gaze follows the torch with saccades; brow -0.4

actions.action: Turns to the foreman and turns both palms up
A thought balloon with a coin pile pops over w1 and is struck out, then deflates

scenes.summary: Then they found it: a blow breaks through into a hidden niche and gold light floods the passage.

scenes.summary: The reckoning. The find is weighed against the cost on a great balance: the two counters stop on the same number and the beam settles dead level.

camera.notes: {x 500, y 700, zoom 1.25} on the scale with caliph and vizier either side; slow push to zoom 1.5 from 79.1 to 82.3; hold on the level beam; a 2 frame hold-still at 84.26.

Caliph at x 160, vizier at x 850. Tags above each pan in panel space; the equals sign appears between them at (500, 420). The opened tunnel mouth (dig 1) is visible behind.

Turns for one last look up the pyramid
actions.acting: gaze climbs to the apex; respect now, not greed (brow -0.3, mouth closed)

actions.action: Pulls out: the red dashed demolition outline reappears over the pyramid, flickers and is wiped off with one stroke
actions.library: CAM keys + outline alpha 1..0 with a wipe line

actions.action: Shakes his head and waves the idea away with the back of his hand
Raises a flat palm to the workers
STOP! as lettering; w2 drops his shovel first and at once, w1 last and reluctantly
actions.acting: w2 delighted (first real smile), w1 looks at the scar once more
actions.library: S.label + stagger(i); tools fall with fallY and a small bounce

actions.action: The caliph mounts; the horse turns to face left
actions.library: rideOn + headTurn then flip under a 2 frame squeeze

actions.action: Rides out left with the vizier and the loaded camel behind; in a small thought balloon over him a throne and a scroll replace the pyramid
actions.acting: gaze ahead, composed; the vizier looks back once
actions.library: rideOn + walk; thoughtCloud with the Library throne anchor drawing and a scroll

scenes.summary: The tale goes on: a wonder of the world, built of huge stones set exactly on one another. The courses build themselves; a blade cannot enter the joint.

camera.notes: Open on the storyteller inset bottom left for 2 s, then crane up the wall {x 560, y 420, zoom 1.2} as the blocks land; close on one joint {x 560, y 730, zoom 3.0} from 117.0.

scenes.composition: Storyteller as a round inset (r 130) at panel bottom left (x 170, y 1040 world) for 107.66 to 110.6, hands telling. The wall is shown empty above course 1 at first; blocks drop into courses 2 to 4. The builder stands on course 0 top (y 730) at x 470 for the blade gag.

actions.action: Round inset irises open: the old storyteller, mid-sentence, one finger raised
actions.acting: twinkle, talk 0.6, gaze to camera then up at the picture
actions.library: inset circle (clip + iris) + PERSON_HANDS.pointUp, sit 1 seat 'floor'

actions.action: Sweeps his hand up toward the wall and the inset slides away
actions.acting: eyes follow his own hand upward

actions.action: Banner WONDER OF THE WORLD unrolls across the top; a ring of small star glints circles the wall
Building replay: the upper courses are empty sky, and blocks begin to drop in one by one from above
actions.acting: each block lands with a 2 frame squash of 6 percent and a dust line
actions.library: fallY + impactSquash per block, seeded order

actions.action: A builder at s 0.8 guides a block down with both hands raised: the block is taller than he is
actions.acting: gaze up at the block, braced knees (sq 0.95)
actions.library: aL, aR raised; lookAt the block

actions.action: A height arrow beside builder and block compares them
The last block slides the final few units sideways and seats with no gap at all
actions.library: kfn ease out + a single joint line

actions.action: Close on the joint: he tries to push a thin blade into it; the blade bends into an arc and springs out of his hand
actions.acting: tongue out in concentration, then eyes follow the blade flying off
actions.library: handRW + a blade drawn as a bending line; knife on an arc

actions.action: Gives the joint a pat and a proud nod to the camera

scenes.summary: Iron and lead in the building (a clamp set in a joint and sealed), then the passages and chambers whose secrets nobody knows.

camera.notes: Macro insert of the joint full frame from 119.62 to 124.9 (ironClamp prop drawn in panel space); cut to the cutaway {x 500, y 560, zoom 1.3} at 124.9 and pull out to 1.0 by 128.9.

scenes.composition: Insert: joint vertical at panel centre, slot across it; clamp enters from the top, ladle from the upper right. Cutaway: chambers A (500, 560), B (420, 690), C (610, 740) appear as dashed shapes with a question mark in each.

actions.action: Macro: two block corners and the hairline joint; a bow-tie slot is chalked across the joint and cut (it darkens)
The dark iron clamp drops into the slot and seats with a 2 frame bounce; label IRON with a pointer
A ladle swings in and pours pale molten lead round the clamp; label LEAD
A builder hand taps the set joint with a mallet twice: nothing moves
actions.acting: only the hand and the mallet in frame
actions.library: strike cycle (small) on a hand + mallet

actions.action: A glint runs along the joint, sealed
Cut to the cutaway of the whole pyramid, solid and dark
Dashed passages snake through the mass like a maze being guessed at
Three dashed chambers pop along the passages, staggered
A question mark pops in each chamber, one after another
The chambers darken to black with the question marks still showing: nobody has seen inside

scenes.summary: The old storytellers claim: jewels, weapons and books in the chambers, and unseen guardians keeping them from time. Told by the fire, pictured in a big story cloud.

camera.notes: Full world to place the fire, the listeners and the pyramid silhouette; from 132.5 the story cloud (thoughtCloud 620 x 400 centred (560, 400)) is the stage; push in on the cloud {x 560, y 460, zoom 1.35} at 138.4 for the guardians.

scenes.composition: Storyteller at x 330 seated, facing right; kid1 x 600 and kid2 x 700 seated facing him; fire at x 500 between them. The cloud rises from the storyteller (tail at his head) and holds the three dashed chambers in a row at scale 0.9: A left, B centre, C right.

actions.action: By the fire at night; he leans in and lowers his voice
actions.acting: firelight flicker on his face, lid 0.3, talk 0.5, gaze on the children

actions.action: Both children lean in; kid1 hugs his knees
actions.acting: eyes wide, kid2 with one brow up

actions.action: The story cloud puffs up from the storyteller: trail first, then the cloud with three dark chambers in it
Chamber A lights: cut gems sparkle
Chamber B lights: crossed swords over a shield
actions.acting: kid1 flinches a little and grins

actions.action: Chamber C lights: a stack of books, one open
actions.acting: kid2 leans forward at last: this is the one she wants

actions.action: Raises both hands with spread fingers and widens his eyes: now the guardians
In the dark passages between the chambers pairs of pale eyes open, one pair after another, and a faint outline of a tall figure forms round one pair and fades again
actions.acting: the eyes blink out of step; they look at the children
actions.library: ghostForm (planned) at low alpha: eye pairs + outline

actions.action: The pale figures drift in front of the three chamber mouths and stand guard
Kid1 hides behind kid2; an hourglass icon at the cloud edge runs and runs, and the chambers do not change
actions.acting: kid2 pats his head without looking away

scenes.summary: The honest note: these are legends in the story, not confirmed facts about the real history of the pyramids. The cloud becomes outlines and is stamped; the real pyramid stays solid behind.

camera.notes: From the cloud {zoom 1.35} back to the full world by 143.3; at 150.3 drift right and up {x 620, y 560, zoom 1.2} to favour the real pyramid silhouette under the moon.

scenes.composition: Cloud at (560, 400) as before. The stamp sits diagonally across the cloud centre. The real pyramid silhouette is at the right behind (apex (700, 330)); when the cloud pops it is left alone in the frame with the moon at (860, 200).

actions.action: Drops his spooky hands, sits back and laughs kindly
Everything inside the cloud loses its colour and becomes dashed outlines: gems, swords, books, guardians
A red rubber stamp thumps diagonally across the cloud: LEGEND
actions.acting: the cloud squashes 5 percent under the stamp and springs back
actions.library: S.label rotated in a red box + impactSquash

actions.action: Kid1 comes out from behind kid2, relieved, and laughs
Taps the side of his head, then opens his hand toward the cloud: it is in the story
The cloud shrinks toward his head and pops, leaving three small puffs
Label NOT PROVEN FACT appears small beside the place where the cloud was
Drifts to the real pyramid: a plain, solid silhouette with a moonlit edge
actions.acting: all three turn their heads to look at it, one after another

actions.action: A single question mark stays on the real pyramid and fades

scenes.summary: The tale ends in reflection: the monuments stay after their owners vanish. An ancient king and his builders stand before the pyramid and blow away as sand while the days race overhead.

camera.notes: Full world, a very slow drift right (x 480 to 520) across the whole scene so the land never feels frozen; no cuts.

scenes.composition: Great pyramid centred right as in S1. The king stands at x 330 (s 0.5) on the sand before it with two builders at x 420 and 480. Sun and moon arc over the apex. No scar on the pyramid in this scene (it is the distant past) until 163.0.

actions.action: Dawn over the pyramids, long shadows; quiet
actions.library: pyramidSite far, skyCycle u 0.02, scar off

actions.action: The shadow of the great pyramid swings slowly across the sand as the sun climbs
actions.library: a shadow polygon keyed from u

actions.action: An ancient king and two builders fade in before the pyramid, tiny against it, looking up at what they made
actions.acting: king proud, hands on hips; builders wipe their brows

actions.action: The pyramid gets a firm outline pulse: it stays
The builders turn to sand from the head down and stream away on the wind, one then the other
actions.acting: no fear: they simply look at the pyramid until they are gone

actions.action: Their tools lie on the sand a moment, then the sand covers them
actions.library: mallet shapes + a rising sand line

actions.action: Days begin to race: sun, moon, sun, moon over the apex
The king blows away last; his gold circlet drops to the sand, rolls and falls flat
actions.acting: gaze up to the apex to the end, lid slowly closing
actions.library: sandBlow + a circlet on a damped roll

actions.action: Sand drifts over the circlet; the empty desert and the pyramid remain
actions.library: sand line + dust dots from K.noise

scenes.summary: The pyramids remain as witnesses to a distant age, and al-Maamun, a small rider under them, stops looking for profit beneath their stones. THE END.

camera.notes: Same far view; the racing sky slows to a warm dusk (u 0.45). Slow pull-out feeling by a 4 percent zoom from 1.04 to 1.0 over 164 to 172. Final frame held from 173.5.

scenes.composition: The three pyramids in dusk light; the scar, a tiny dark arch at (300, 900), now visible on the great pyramid. Caliph, vizier and camel cross the foreground right to left at s 0.42 along y 930. THE END sits in the sky upper left (x 90..470, y 150..300), clear of the apex.

actions.action: The racing sky brakes and settles into a golden dusk
Outline pulses run over the three pyramids, largest first
A caravan of three tiny camel silhouettes passes far behind, then a single later traveller: ages of visitors
Stars come out early above the apex and one glint sits on the tip
Al-Maamun rides in from the right at small scale, the vizier and the loaded camel behind
Halts level with the scar
actions.acting: horse ears forward; he turns his head to the little tunnel mouth

actions.action: A small arrow points at the scar: his tunnel, a pinprick on the mass
A coin balloon pops over his head; he waves it away himself and it bursts
Bows his head to the pyramid, one hand on his chest
actions.acting: eyes closed for 8 frames, then open

actions.action: He rides on to the left; the long shadows of the pyramids lie over the riders as they go
After the last word THE END pops in the sky upper left
Hold: riders leave the frame, the pyramids keep still, a little sand blows across the scar

ending.description: Dusk over the three pyramids with the tiny tunnel scar; the caliph bows his head and rides out left with vizier and camel. THE END pops in the sky upper left at 173.66 and is held to 177.86 (end_hold 4.0) while sand blows across the scar.

subtitles.ar: تحكي رواية قديمة أن الخليفة المأمون وصل إلى مصر،|وشاهد الأهرامات العظيمة، فدهش من ضخامة أحجارها وارتفاعها.|سمع أن الناس يتحدثون عن كنوز مخبأة داخلها،|فأراد أن يعرف ما تخفيه.
subtitles.en: An old tale says Caliph al-Maamun visited Egypt|and marveled at the pyramids.|Hearing rumors of hidden treasure,|he wanted to discover what lay inside.

subtitles.ar: قرر المأمون فتح أحد الأهرامات،|بل حاول إزالة جزء كبير منه. جمع العمال وأمرهم بالحفر،|لكن الحجارة الضخمة قاومت أدواتهم، وكان العمل أبطأ وأصعب مما توقع الجميع في البداية.
subtitles.en: Al-Maamun ordered workers to open a pyramid|and even tried to take part of it down.|Its enormous stones resisted their tools.

subtitles.ar: استمر العمل أيامًا كثيرة، وأنفق الخليفة مبالغ ضخمة على الرجال والأدوات ونقل الحجارة.|ومع ذلك لم يتمكن العمال إلا من فتح نفق صغير في جسم الهرم،|ولم يظهر لهم ما كانوا يتوقعونه.
subtitles.en: Work continued at great cost,|but the laborers managed to open only a small tunnel.|The expected riches did not readily appear.

subtitles.ar: ثم وجدوا، كما تقول الحكاية، مالًا وكنوزًا داخل الممر.|أمر المأمون بحساب قيمتها ومقارنتها بما دفعه للحفر،|فكانت المفاجأة أن القيمة ساوت نفقات العمل تمامًا، لا أكثر ولا أقل.
subtitles.en: Eventually, the story says, treasure was found.|Its value matched exactly what the caliph had spent|on excavation—no more and no less.

subtitles.ar: تعجب الخليفة من هذا الاتفاق الغريب، وأدرك أنه لم يربح شيئًا من محاولته المكلفة.|أخذ ما وجده،|ثم ترك فكرة هدم الأهرامات، وأمر بوقف العمل والعودة إلى شؤون الحكم الأخرى.
subtitles.en: Astonished by the coincidence and his lack of profit,|the caliph took what had been discovered|and abandoned his attempt to dismantle the pyramids.

subtitles.ar: تواصل الرواية وصف الأهرامات بأنها من عجائب الدنيا،|مبنية من أحجار عظيمة وضعت بدقة فوق بعضها.|وتتحدث عن حديد ورصاص استعملا في البناء، وعن ممرات وغرف لا يعرف الناس أسرارها.
subtitles.en: The tale describes the pyramids as wonders|built from immense, carefully fitted stones,|and imagines mysterious passages and chambers within them.

subtitles.ar: ويزعم الرواة القدماء أن بعض الغرف تضم جواهر وأسلحة وكتبًا،|وأن حراسًا خفيين يحفظونها من الزمان.|هذه أوصاف أسطورية وردت في القصة،|وليست معلومات مؤكدة عن تاريخ الأهرامات الحقيقي.
subtitles.en: Ancient storytellers imagined jewels, weapons, writings|and unseen guardians inside.|These are legendary claims,|not established facts about the pyramids.

subtitles.ar: وتنتهي الحكاية بالتأمل في الآثار التي بقيت بعدما اختفى أصحابها.|فقد رحل الملوك والبناؤون، وظلت الأهرامات تشهد على زمن بعيد،|بينما توقف المأمون عن البحث عن ربح تحت حجارتها.
subtitles.en: The tale closes by reflecting on monuments that outlast their builders.|Kings passed away, pyramids endured,|and al-Maamun stopped seeking profit beneath their stones.

new_assets.name: pyramidSite
new_assets.description: One module with three views of the same pyramid: 'far' (three pyramids on Library dunes with skyCycle, scar option), 'face' (close stepped wall of big blocks with dig 0..1 and outline 0..1) and 'section' (cutaway with tunnel len, niche breach, legend chambers, solid). All dimensions are in the sets entries pyramidFar, pyramidFace, pyramidSection. Reusable for any Egypt, tomb, treasure or ruin tale.
new_assets.implementation: sets/pyramid.js: pyramidSite(ctx, {view, u, dig, outline, len, breach, legend, solid, scar, camX}) returning anchors {apex, base, digBlock, mouth, tunnelEnd, niche, chambers}. Static parts baked with bake() per view and option set; faces are polygons with Ben-Day dot fills (S dots helper), course lines and joints from a seeded loop, brush outline. far reuses the desertRoad dune layers (road false) and palmTree. Keyed parts (dig hole, outline dash, tunnel length, breach wall, legend dashes with lineDashOffset) drawn live.

new_assets.name: desertCamp
new_assets.description: The planned campsite (AN-044, AN-124), used here in its night state with one tent, the fire and the carpet mat, plus a pyramid silhouette option. See sets.campNight.
new_assets.implementation: If desertCamp exists by then, call it with night and add the silhouette polygon; otherwise draw skyCycle(u 0.72), two dune curves, a striped tent (triangle fan), a fire (three flame paths scaled by K.noise, a radial halftone disc) and a carpet rectangle.

new_assets.name: pickaxe
new_assets.description: Pickaxe with a bend field (see props). Used with the planned shovel and torch.
new_assets.implementation: props: a rounded rect shaft and a curved double-point head as one path, rotated about the grip; bend rotates the outer third of one point. Icon mode for the broken-tool heap.

new_assets.name: balanceScale
new_assets.description: The planned balance scale at large size with a tilt field and pans that take content callbacks (see props).
new_assets.implementation: Post and foot as rects; beam rotated by tilt about the pivot; pan positions from the beam ends, chains as three lines, pans as shallow arcs; content drawn by callback at the pan centre.

new_assets.name: treasureHoard
new_assets.description: The planned chest (lid, fill), with the planned coinPile and jewels: used as the pay chest and as the found hoard.
new_assets.implementation: Reuse the planned functions; chest = box + arched lid rotated about the back hinge, coins as overlapping ellipses above the rim scaled by fill.

new_assets.name: ironClamp
new_assets.description: Macro joint insert with a bow-tie iron clamp and poured lead (see props).
new_assets.implementation: Panel-space drawing: two block fills, a bow-tie polygon slot, the same polygon in blue-grey falling with fallY, a lead fill polygon clipped to the slot whose top edge is a sine line that flattens with fill; ladle as arc plus handle.

new_assets.name: ledger
new_assets.description: The planned account book with tally strokes (AN-138).
new_assets.implementation: Two page quads, strokes in rows of five by fill.

new_assets.name: priceTags
new_assets.description: The planned running-total tags: SPENT, FOUND and PROFIT with coin icons, counting on keyed times.
new_assets.implementation: Panel-space S.box + S.counter with kfn values; the equals sign and EXACTLY! as S.label.

new_assets.name: goldGlow
new_assets.description: The planned treasure light: rays, halftone disc, staggered glints, strength 0..1.
new_assets.implementation: As planned by KD-031; clip it to the tunnel and niche shape in the section view.

new_assets.name: sandBlow
new_assets.description: The planned effect (AN-088) that turns a drawn figure into sand streaming away: the gentle way to show that kings and builders are gone.
new_assets.implementation: Draw the figure to an offscreen canvas; p 0..0.3 tint to one sand tone; p 0.3..1 clip away everything above a wipe line and emit seeded dots (K.rng by index) that drift sideways and fade as a pure function of t.

new_assets.name: ghostForm
new_assets.description: The planned vision treatment (AN-082, AN-114), used very lightly: pale eye pairs and a faint outline of a tall figure for the unseen guardians.
new_assets.implementation: Eye pairs as two white ellipses with pupils (eye2) and seeded blinks; outline = a person silhouette stroked dashed at alpha 0.35 with a wavy hem.

new_assets.name: inset circle
new_assets.description: The planned round picture-in-picture with an iris, for the storyteller at 107.66.
new_assets.implementation: Circular clip with a brush ring; radius eased 0 to 130.

new_assets.name: strikeCycle
new_assets.description: The guide's strike cycle (Fox branch) applied to a person with a pickaxe: lift 0.3 s, whip down, contact on the cue, damped rebound; a slow variant with doubled period for fatigue.
new_assets.implementation: A function of (t, hits) returning arm angles aL, aR and tool rot; contact times listed in S5; rebound from rebound().

owner_questions: SCRIPT: the English is a condensed translation, not sentence for sentence (for example P2 omits that the work was slower and harder than expected, P3 omits the spending on men, tools and hauling, P5 omits stopping the work and returning to affairs of rule, P6 omits iron and lead); both are kept verbatim.
SCRIPT: the English of P4 contains an em dash (excavation, no more and no less); it is kept verbatim in the subtitle although on-screen text normally avoids dashes. Default: keep verbatim.
The sums are shown as invented round counters (SPENT 100 and FOUND 100 purses, PROFIT 0); the script gives no numbers. Default: use 100 with a coin icon and no currency name.
P6 and P7 are staged as an old storyteller telling children by a fire (an addition), so that the legends are visibly a tale. Default: keep the storyteller frame.
The unseen guardians are shown only as pale eye pairs and a faint outline inside the story cloud, not as monsters. Default: keep them gentle.
In P8 an ancient king and builders (generic, no named pharaoh, no Egyptian religious imagery) blow away as sand to show that the owners are gone. Default: use the sand effect, no graves or bones.

Added gags beyond the script: the pick that curls into a hook, the blade that cannot enter the joint, the last coin falling from the upturned pay chest, the caliph bowing his head to the pyramid at the end. Default: keep all four.

Invented lettering (20 items in all): EGYPT, OPEN IT!, CLANG!, DAY 30, SPENT, TINY!, GOLD!, FOUND, =, EXACTLY!, PROFIT 0, STOP!, WONDER OF THE WORLD, IRON, LEAD, ? ? ?, LEGEND, NOT PROVEN FACT, plus the title and THE END. Default: use as listed.
implementation_notes: Timeline: every cue is a word start from planning/inputs/timeline.md on the final MP3 (173.86 s). Film length 177.86 s (end_hold 4.0).

The narration has no pauses of 0.6 s or more; the only gap is 66.68 to 67.20. Use three effects only: a soft chime at 66.94 (the wall breaks), a chime at 173.66 and a quiet whoosh at 175.0 under THE END. All impacts (CLANG!, blocks landing, the stamp) are silent and carried by lettering and squash.
Build pyramidSite first (three views, one module) and check each view as a still with a person beside it for scale before staging.

People: Library person with costume presets only (caliph, vizier, villager, servant, carpenter, villageWoman, ascetic, prince, child). Set LIFE.t = t each frame for auto blinks; set noBlink on the caliph from 80.16 to 83.7.

Tools in hands: draw the pickaxe, shovel, torch and ledger at P.hands (returned by person) after the figure; for the strike use arm angles aL, aR (about [2.45, 2.85] raised) so the pose reads at phone size, not hand targets near the head.
Workers never move in unison: w1 leads, w3 follows 3 to 4 frames later, w2 6 to 8 frames later (stagger(i)); different strike phases in the S6 time-lapse.

S6 is a locked shot: only skyCycle u, the shadow, the chest fill, the dig field and the counters change. Animate u with kfn from 0.2 to 3.2 between 43.2 and 46.4, then hold day (u 0.25 equivalent) for the coin beats.
Section view figures are at s 0.24: keep the camera at zoom 2.4 or more whenever they act (S7 from 61.2, S8 throughout) so they are at least about 135 px tall on screen.

S9 scale: beam tilt = 0.22 while only FOUND is loaded, then swing(t, 78.3, ...) decaying to exactly 0 at 82.32; the two finger presses at 85.78 and 86.88 are tilt pulses of plus and minus 0.06 that return to 0.
Counters and tags are drawn in panel space (not world) so camera pushes do not move them; keep them above y 420 of the panel and never over a face.
Camera cuts under the LATER card at 65.06: put two CAM keys 0.01 s apart at the covered midpoint.
Panel-only shake (template) for the three strikes in S5; the caption panel never moves.
Subtitles: chunks_ar.txt and chunks_en.txt from the subtitles array (verbatim, 3 or 4 chunks per paragraph).
Ending: THE END in the upper left sky (x 90..470, y 150..300 world), clear of the apex at (560, 250) and of the riders.
warnings: No real pauses in the narration: resist adding sound effects inside words.
P6 to P8 (66 s) have no plot; the plan gives them their own pictures (building replay, clamp insert, fireside legends, sand and time). Keep something changing every 1 to 2 s there.
pyramidSite is a large new set (three views). If time is short, build face and far first; the section view can share the outline code.
The front-facing person cannot swing a pick in profile: sell the strike with arm angles, tool rotation, body tip and the contact effects.
Tiny figures in the far view (s 0.42 to 0.5) are for scale only; do not put acting that matters on them except the final bow, which is helped by the arrow and the balloon.
Keep the depiction of the caliph respectful: he is curious and proud, never a buffoon; the joke is on the arithmetic.
